oracle.expected: The Package A contract or implementation artifact explicitly names the existing Phase isolation/recovery and Quick Dev evidence-writing authorities and shows Package A delegates to them without reimplementing or replacing either boundary.
forbidden: Package A takes over Phase isolation or recovery.
Package A takes over Quick Dev evidence writing.
oracle.observable: A contract or boundary check contains explicit authority references and demonstrates delegation to the existing Phase and Quick Dev owners.

acceptance.then: The Package A contract preserves those authority boundaries and contains no replacement Phase isolation/recovery or Quick Dev evidence-writing implementation.
acceptance.when: During contract review and targeted validation of the Package A standard and validator boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A declared Package A boundary test detects a contract or implementation assigning Phase isolation/recovery or Quick Dev evidence-writing authority to Package A and raises AssertionError when replacement ownership is present.

affected_subjects: Existing Phase and Quick Dev authorities
slice_hint.behavior_change: Document and validate that Package A remains a read-only declaration and structure validator while existing Phase isolation/recovery and Quick Dev evidence writers retain authority.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Remove only Package A boundary declarations and validator changes; preserve existing Phase isolation/recovery, Quick Dev evidence writers, and existing protocols.

slice_hint.state_transition: Existing Phase and Quick Dev authority boundaries remain unchanged while Package A adds declarative validation and documentation of those boundaries.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted boundary assertion passes only when Package A names and delegates to the existing Phase isolation/recovery and Quick Dev evidence-writing authorities, with forbidden takeover patterns absent.
